claim: Select a theme with `page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme })` and nothing else. Do NOT write `data-theme`, and do NOT drive the app's own theme control.
evidence: Measured against http://localhost:3003/pricing: emulateMedia('light') gives body background rgb(250,249,247), emulateMedia('dark') gives rgb(18,18,17), and `documentElement.getAttribute('data-theme')` stays null in both. docs/DESIGN.md puts the dark values behind `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])`, so the media path is the whole job. Writing data-theme fights the app's own theme script; a single click on the theme control only OPENS a dropdown, which is how a half-dark frame came to be reported as a product defect three times in one run.
invalidatesWhen: docs/DESIGN.md stops guaranteeing the media-query path, or `applyTheme` in e2e/helpers/shoot.ts changes

claim: Resolve the dev server with `scripts/ultrabuild/resolve-port.sh` (add `--start` if you are allowed to start one). Never probe the pool by hand, never assume 3000, never kill a server you did not start.
evidence: The rule used to be prose in four prompts and produced 23 port findings across ten rounds. Sixteen concurrent `pnpm dev` servers once put this machine at load average 563 with 4.4 GB of swap, and round 4's gate returned 64 failures of which none was a pixel difference. The script probes /api/dev/seed, which is this repo's own endpoint, so a match proves the server is ours rather than merely alive.
invalidatesWhen: the pool bounds change, or /api/dev/seed stops answering on a dev build

claim: Take blind-pair frames with `scripts/ultrabuild/capture.mjs`. It owns the viewport, the theme, animation suppression, the map-ready wait, the filename and the console classification.
evidence: The procedure used to be ~2 KB of prose that each capture agent re-derived. Cost across two runs: 5 findings about a wrongly switched theme, frames shot with the screen at rest when a hover state was under judgement, flat-colour frames from a WebGL canvas photographed before its first idle, and 36 findings about scratch PNGs left at the repo root.
invalidatesWhen: the script stops covering a state the item needs — extend the script, do not go around it

claim: Our authenticated screens are photographed with Playwright, which holds the demo session in e2e/.auth/demo.json. Ego Lite cannot reach them. A stale session does not fail, it redirects to /login — refresh it with `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL=http://localhost:<port> pnpm exec playwright test --project=setup`.
evidence: Measured: an Ego tab opening /atlas lands on /login?redirect=%2Fatlas, and signing in from inside the task space did not work (no input[type=email], pageInfo() timed out, tab ended on about:blank). Measured again during this review: a cached demo.json against a freshly started server on 3003 redirected /atlas to /login, so the guard in capture.mjs refuses to file that frame.
measuredIn: atlas-tooltips run, rounds 9-12 and post-round-12 review
invalidatesWhen: someone demonstrates Ego Lite carrying our session, with a measurement

claim: A page with a MapLibre canvas is ready when at least one `[data-map-ready]` marker exists AND no `[data-map-ready="false"]` remains. Wait again after every resize and every theme change.
evidence: `settleMap()` in e2e/helpers/shoot.ts makes the same two-sided check, for the same reason: a bare wait on `[data-map-ready="true"]` hangs, because the marker sits on a wrapper Playwright does not always call visible. A theme change replaces the whole style document through setStyle and the marker goes back to false.

claim: A Playwright or vitest failure whose message is a TIMEOUT, with no pixel count and no assertion diff, is evidence about this machine's load and not about the code. Report it; never change code in response to one.
evidence: src/lib/map/__tests__/countries.test.ts timing out at 5000ms is the standing example: it passes 74/74 when run alone. 12 findings in the current run and 10 in the previous one were timeouts of this shape.
invalidatesWhen: a timeout reproduces on an idle machine

claim: A console message whose own stack frame is a Vite dev-server namespace (/@vite/, /@react-refresh, /@id/, /@fs/) is the toolchain talking, not the application. It is not a defect of the item under judgement.
evidence: `ReferenceError: document is not defined` from http://localhost:3001/@vite/client:976 (handleMessage) failed atlas-country-actions and atlas-country-card in round 9. Both were otherwise finished. The gate itself never sees it, because the gate runs no dev client — see TOLERATED_CONSOLE_WARNINGS in e2e/helpers/shoot.ts, which must stay as strict as it is.
invalidatesWhen: the message originates from our own bundle rather than from a dev-server namespace

claim: `pnpm check` (prettier) fails repo-wide on ~157 pre-existing files and is deliberately not part of the mechanical gate. Keep the files you touch prettier-clean; never reformat the repo as a side effect.
evidence: Standing decision, carried in the /ultrabuild command since the first run.
invalidatesWhen: someone formats the repo as its own task

claim: Every screenshot belongs under .claude/ultrabuild/shots/<slug>/round-<n>/<item-id>/, every scratch script in the session scratchpad. Delete what you created once it has served its purpose.
evidence: One run left eleven loose PNGs and two probe scripts at the repo root and a `git add -A` committed 770 KB of them. 36 findings in the current run and 17 in the previous one were about stray artefacts. A root-level PNG/mjs rule in .gitignore is the backstop, not the fix.
invalidatesWhen: never — this is a convention, not a measurement

claim: `extraHTTPHeaders` in playwright.config.ts applies the x-pt-server-today clock pin to EVERY request the context makes, including cross-origin Google Fonts, which rejects the preflight. Every baseline in e2e/__screenshots__ is therefore recorded in the fallback face. Scope the header to the app origin.
evidence: Reported by the auditor of atlas-country-actions: 'Request header field x-pt-server-today is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Headers'. scripts/ultrabuild/capture.mjs scopes it per-request for exactly this reason.
invalidatesWhen: playwright.config.ts scopes the header, which is open backlog work

claim: The blind critic judges the whole SCREEN, not the component the item owns. Screen-level defects — the 360px composition, a panel's information architecture, a card clipped by its scroll container — will surface while an item that owns none of those files is under judgement.
evidence: In the atlas run, atlas-country-card was repeatedly rejected for defects belonging to src/routes/_app/-ui/atlas-screen.tsx, which it does not own. A component item can only reach acceptance once the screen hosting it is finished, so order the items that way and put the screen-level acceptance on the item that owns the screen.
invalidatesWhen: the capture starts cropping to the item's own element, which it does not

claim: For an item whose point is an interaction state, the capture must photograph THAT state. Declare it in the item's captureStates so scripts/ultrabuild/capture.mjs reaches it; a resting-screen frame is not evidence about such an item.
evidence: Every blind pair in rounds 1-5 of the atlas run photographed /atlas at rest. The critic accepted atlas-map-overlay at high confidence without ever seeing the hover tooltip, which was the entire thing the user had asked for.
invalidatesWhen: never — it is a property of judging by pictures

claim: The dependsOn edges in .claude/ultrabuild/recon/gap-rows.json are NOT a DAG and cannot be topologically sorted as written — they contain nine mutual A->B / B->A pairs. Any wave ordering must cut edges explicitly and record which ones it cut.
evidence: Measured by the plan-index builder in round 1 while deriving the wave table. A naive topological sort lands TRP-11 in wave 4 and disagrees with the recon summary, which names it one of four wave-1 leaders.
invalidatesWhen: gap-rows.json is rewritten with an acyclic dependsOn

claim: New markdown under docs/ passes pnpm lint untouched — eslint never sees it — but hand-written markdown is NOT prettier-clean: prettier rewrites table column padding and converts *emphasis* to _emphasis_. Run pnpm exec prettier --write on every markdown file you create.
evidence: Measured in round 1 on docs/plans/README.md and docs/plans/TEMPLATE.md.

claim: The repo-wide Playwright gate is RED at HEAD c97dfd1 for reasons that predate this run: 44 failed / 5 skipped / 88 passed. typecheck, lint, 2243 unit tests and build are all green. NO item in this run can turn it green, because every item owns only docs/ and every failure is in a src/-rendered screen. Items therefore settle at accepted-pending-gate, and this run must never report the gate as passed.
evidence: git diff 54f18a7..HEAD -- e2e playwright.config.ts src is EMPTY, so neither the app nor the gate config changed since the baselines were recorded, when the gate was 105/105 green on 2026-08-21. The working tree carries only untracked docs/plans/*.md. Failure shapes: pricing-light 76px taller, legal-terms 283px, legal-privacy 118px, dashboard-light, trips-light, mobile-safari landing, plus a functional [data-part="country-panel"] that never renders and chrome.shelf null on /atlas. The measuring agent recorded that NONE of the 44 is a load-related timeout — every one carries a pixel count or a concrete missing-locator assertion.
invalidatesWhen: the gate goes green, or a source change lands that could plausibly explain the failures

claim: The workflow's in-round repair pass is guarded on `mechanicalGreen`. While the repo gate stays red, a rejected item gets exactly ONE build attempt per round and no same-round retry, so every rejection costs a whole round. Budget maxRounds accordingly rather than assuming three attempts per item.
evidence: Read at .claude/workflows/ultrabuild.js line 1230: the `while` loop requires itemRound < MAX_ITEM_ROUNDS AND rejected items AND mechanicalGreen. Rounds 1 and 2 each carried exactly one build of plan-index-and-conventions.
invalidatesWhen: the repo gate goes green, or the guard changes

claim: An item with neither `url` nor `referenceUrl` is NOT penalised for having no visual verdict — verdictFor() guards that reason behind `else if (item.url || item.referenceUrl)`. A documentation item is therefore judged by the auditor alone, and only BLOCKING audit findings reject it; minor ones are recorded and carried.
evidence: Read at .claude/workflows/ultrabuild.js lines 1163-1172. Confirmed by round 2, where plan-index-and-conventions was rejected with the single reason "1 blocking audit finding(s)" while carrying five minor ones.
invalidatesWhen: verdictFor() stops guarding the visual reason on url/referenceUrl
